title: Conventions
body_md: The letter $\mu$ is reserved for the joint distribution on a product $\Sigma_1\times\cdots\times\Sigma_m$ of alphabets, such as the distribution detecting our configurations. A probability measure on a \emph{single} alphabet $\Sigma$ is denoted by $\pi$. In our application every $\Sigma_j$ is $\mathbb{F}_p$, and every marginal of $\mu$ is the uniform measure on $\mathbb{F}_p$ (Lemma \ref{l;large exp}), so $\pi$ will be the uniform measure. The letter $\alpha$ always denotes the density of a set, and $T$ always denotes the translation operator $Tf(x)=f(x+1)$.
head: manual

title: Definition
body_md: For $0< \rho < 1$, the \textit{$\rho$-correlated distribution} on $(\Sigma, \pi)$ is defined as follows. For $x\in \Sigma$, we write $y \sim_{\rho} x$ to indicate that $y$ is randomly chosen as follows: with probability $\rho$ we set $y=x$, and with probability $1- \rho$ we draw $y \sim \pi$ independently of $x$. Given a function $f \colon \Sigma \to \mathbb{C}$, we set $N_ \rho f (x) \coloneqq \mathbb{E}_{y\sim_{\rho} x} f(y)$, the \textit{\( \rho   \)-noise operator}. On $\Sigma^n$ with the product measure $\pi^{\otimes n}$, we use the same symbol $N_\rho$ for the tensor product operator $N_\rho^{\otimes n}$, which applies the noise independently in each coordinate.

title: Definition
body_md:
The \textit{Efron-Stein decomposition} of a function $f \colon \Sigma^n \to \mathbb{C}$
  with respect to $\pi^{\otimes n}$ is defined in terms of a decomposition of \( L^2(\Sigma^n, \pi^{\otimes n}) \).
  For \( S \subseteq [n] \), set  \( V_S \) to be all functions \( f \) which are of the form
  \( f(x) = g(x|_S) \), for some function \( g \colon \Sigma^S \to \mathbb{C} \).
  Then, define \(  V _{\subseteq S}  \) to be the span of \( \{ V_{S'} \colon S'\subseteq S\}\).
  The subspace \( V_{=S} = V_{\subseteq S} \cap \bigcap_{T'\subsetneqq S} V_{\subseteq T'} ^{\perp}   \).
  It can be shown that the spaces \( V_{=S} \) are pairwise orthogonal, and hence
  \( L^2(\Sigma^n)= \bigoplus _{S\subseteq [n]} V _{=S}   \).
  The orthogonal projection of \( f \) onto \( V_{=S}  \) is given by
 \begin{align}
    f^{=S}(x_S)  = \sum_{S'\subseteq S} (-1) ^{\lvert S\setminus S'\rvert} \mathbb{E}_{\pi^{\otimes \overline{S'}}} (f (y) \mid y|_{S'}=x_{S'}).
 \end{align}
 The \textit{Efron-Stein decomposition} of $f$ is then given by
 \begin{align*}
    f (x) = \sum_{\substack{S \subseteq [n] }} f^{=S} (x_S).
\end{align*}
In particular, $f^{=\emptyset}= \mathbb{E}f $.

label: lem:cyclicReduction
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cyclicReduction}
    Suppose $\mu$ is a probability distribution on a finite set $\Sigma_0  \times \Sigma_1 \times \cdots \times \Sigma_\ell$ which admits a nontrivial abelian embedding into some abelian group. Then there exists a prime $q$ for which $\mu$ admits a nontrivial abelian embedding into the cyclic group $(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z},+)$.

label: lem:kronecker
title: Lemma
body_md: \label{lem:kronecker} Let $K$ be a number field and let $\theta \in K^\times$ be not a root of unity. Then there exists a place $v$ of $K$ such that $|\theta|_v\neq 1$.
head: environment
name: An implication of Kronecker's theorem

title: Proof
body_md: Suppose that $|\theta|_v = 1$ for every place $v$ of $K$. The non-archimedean places show that $\theta$ lies in every localization of $\mathcal{O}_K$ at a prime, so $\theta\in\mathcal{O}_K$ is an algebraic integer. The archimedean places show that every Galois conjugate of $\theta$ has absolute value $1$, since each conjugate is $\iota(\theta)$ for some embedding $\iota$. By Kronecker's theorem, an algebraic integer all of whose conjugates lie on the unit circle is a root of unity, a contradiction.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md: If $K$ is a Noetherian ring (all ideals are finitely generated), then the polynomial ring $K[z]$ is also Noetherian. In particular, $\mathbb{Q}[z]$ is a Noetherian ring.

label: lem:defRankImpliesUnity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:defRankImpliesUnity}
    Suppose $\theta\in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^\times$ is a nonzero algebraic number and $A_{\ell,\infty}(\theta)$ has (column) rank $r$ with $r<\ell$. Then, there exists some positive integer $s$ such that $\theta^s=1$ (i.e. $\theta$ is a root of unity).

title: Proof

label: lem:finitelyManyRowsSuffice
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:finitelyManyRowsSuffice}
    Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $\theta\in K$. Then the matrix  $A_{\ell,M(\ell)}(\theta)$ has rank less than $\ell$ if and only if $A_{\ell,\infty}(\theta)$ has rank less than $\ell$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
($\implies$) Suppose that $A_{\ell,M(\ell)}(\theta)$ has rank less than $\ell$. Then all of its $\ell\times \ell$ minors vanish, and in particular $\Delta(M_{S_i})(\theta)=0$ for $1\leq i\leq t$. Let $S$ be arbitrary. Since $\Delta(M_S)\in I$, we can write $\Delta(M_S)=\sum_{i=1}^t a_i\Delta(M_{S_i})$ with $a_i\in\mathbb{Q}[z]$. Evaluation at $\theta$ is a ring homomorphism $\mathbb{Q}[z]\to K$ (because $K\supseteq\mathbb{Q}$), so $\Delta(M_S)(\theta)=\sum_i a_i(\theta)\Delta(M_{S_i})(\theta)=0$. Thus every $\ell\times \ell$ minor of $A_{\ell,\infty}(\theta)$ vanishes, and $A_{\ell,\infty}(\theta)$ has rank less than $\ell$.

    ($\impliedby$) If $A_{\ell,\infty}(\theta)$ has rank less than $\ell$, then so does its submatrix $A_{\ell,M(\ell)}(\theta)$.

label: lem:goodCharacteristics
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:goodCharacteristics}
    Suppose $q\nmid N$, and that $\lambda \in \overline{\mathbb{F}}_q^\times$ is a root of the reduction of $D(z)=z^a \prod_{m\in \mathcal{E}_\ell}\Phi_m(z)^{e_m}$ modulo $q$ (call this $\overline{D}(z)$). Then, there exists some $m\in \mathcal{E}_\ell$ such that $\lambda^m=1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Since $\lambda\neq 0$, one has that $\lambda$ is the root of some $\overline{\Phi_m}$, with $m\in \mathcal{E}_\ell$. Since $\Phi_m(z)|(z^m-1)$, the same divisibility holds after reducing modulo $q$, and so $\lambda^m=1$.

label: lem:diffChar
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:diffChar}
    Let $M\geq M(\ell)$, let $p>P(\ell)$ be prime, and let $q\neq p$ be prime. If $f_0,\ldots,f_\ell:\mathbb{F}_p\to\mathbb{F}_q$ satisfy \eqref{eq no ab restriction}, then $f_j$ is constant for every $j=0,1,\ldots,\ell$. That is, $\mu$ admits no nontrivial abelian embedding into $(\mathbb{F}_q,+)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $\lambda\in\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q$ satisfy $\lambda^p=1$ and $\lambda\neq 1$. Since $p$ is prime, $\lambda$ has multiplicative order $p$. The matrix $A_{\ell,M}(\lambda)$ contains $A_{\ell,M(\ell)}(\lambda)$ as its first $M(\ell)-1$ rows, and the latter has rank $\ell$ by Proposition \ref{prop:uniformTorsionRank}. Hence $A_{\ell,M}(\lambda)$ has trivial kernel, and $f_{j,\lambda}(0)=0$ for $1\leq j\leq \ell$, that is, $f_{j,\lambda}=0$. Therefore, for $1\leq j\leq \ell$, $f_j=f_{j,1}$ lies in the $1$-eigenspace of $T$, which consists of the constant functions. Finally, the case $y=0$ of \eqref{eq no ab restriction} reads $f_0(x)=-\sum_{j=1}^\ell f_j(x)$, so $f_0$ is constant as well.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Suppose that $\mu$ admits a nontrivial abelian embedding. By Lemma \ref{lem:cyclicReduction}, it then admits a nontrivial abelian embedding $f_0,\ldots,f_\ell:\mathbb{F}_p\to\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ for some prime $q$. Since the support of $\mu$ is the whole set in Proposition \ref{prop:noAbelianEmbeddings}, these maps satisfy $f_0(x)+\sum_{j=1}^\ell f_j(x+y^j)=0$ for all $x\in\mathbb{F}_p$ and all $y\in\{0,2,\ldots,M\}$. If $q=p$, Lemma \ref{lem:sameChar} (which applies since $M\geq \ell+1$ and $p>M$) shows that every $f_j$ is constant. If $q\neq p$, Lemma \ref{lem:diffChar} (which applies since $M\geq M(\ell)$ and $p>P(\ell)$) shows the same. Either way the embedding is trivial, a contradiction.

label: l;stability
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{l;stability}  Let \( \Sigma \) be a finite alphabet with measure \( \pi \). 
For every \( 0< \delta < \frac{1}{2} \), \( n \in \mathbb{N} \), and \(  f \colon \Sigma^n\to  \{0,1\}\),  if \( \operatorname{Stab}_{1- \delta}(f - \mathbb{E}f) > \delta \), then 
\( W_{\leq d} (f- \mathbb{E} f) \geq \frac{\delta}{2} \), for \(  d =O( \frac{1}{\delta} \log  \frac{2}{\delta}) \).

label: l;fiber
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Restrictions preserve the hypothesis

title: Proof
body_md: Suppose that $(v_0, \ldots, v_{k-1})$ is a valid $k$-tuple in $A_{\overline{S} \rightarrow u}$, and define $x_j \in \mathbb{F}_p^n$ by $(x_j)_S = v_j$ and $(x_j)_{\overline{S}} = u$ for $0 \leq j \leq k-1$. Each $x_j$ lies in $A$. For a coordinate $i \in S$, the $i$-th coordinates of $x_0, \ldots, x_{k-1}$ form a tuple in $\operatorname{supp} \mu$ by assumption. For $i \in \overline{S}$ they form the diagonal tuple $(u_i, \ldots, u_i)$, which lies in $\operatorname{supp} \mu$ because $0 \in Y$ (take $x = u_i$ and $y = 0$). Finally, the $x_j$ are not all equal, since the $v_j$ are not. Hence $(x_0, \ldots, x_{k-1})$ is a valid $k$-tuple in $A$, a contradiction.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Lemma \ref{l;fiber} is the reason $0$ is included in $Y$: coordinates frozen by a restriction are filled in with the step $y_i = 0$. In terms of progressions, a nontrivial restricted progression $v, v + P_1(y'), \ldots, v+ P_{k-1}(y')$ in $A_{\overline{S} \rightarrow u}$, with $y' \in Y^S \setminus \{\vec{0}\}$, lifts to the nontrivial restricted progression in $A$ with base point $(v,u)$ and step $(y', \vec{0}) \in Y^n \setminus \{\vec{0}\}$.
